steps.message:
Build an 8-slide, 16:9 analytical presentation titled "Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks: Time Horizon Doubling Every 7 Months" for AI safety researchers, frontier AI lab leadership, and policy analysts tracking autonomous AI capabilities.

The deck should open with the headline finding—50% task-completion time horizon doubling every ~7 months—then walk the audience through the metric methodology, the 170-task suite composition, and the exponential trend from GPT-2 (2 seconds) to o3 (~2 hours). It should then examine per-model success curves, the capability drivers behind the trend, forward extrapolations toward month-long task automation by 2028–2031, and close with safety governance takeaways.

**Visual requirements:**
- Slide 3 ("Task Suite Overview") must include a structured table listing the three task-suite sources (HCAST, RE-Bench, SWAA) with task counts and example tasks spanning 3 seconds to 8 hours.
- Slide 4 ("Exponential Trend") must feature a chart or chart-style visual depicting the 50% time horizon vs. model release date, clearly labeling the ~207-day doubling time, R²=0.97, and key model milestones (GPT-2, GPT-4, o3).

Use a data-forward, technical tone throughout. All figures referenced (figure_1.jpg, figure_2.jpg, figure_3.jpg) should be placed on their corresponding slides where available. Do not fabricate any data not found in source_brief.md.


## Data Sources

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

arguments.content:
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
import os

def create_presentation():
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    # Helper function to add a title slide
    def add_title_slide(title_text, subtitle_text):
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
        title = slide.shapes.title
        subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
        title.text = title_text
        subtitle.text = subtitle_text
        return slide

    # Helper function to add a title and content slide
    def add_content_slide(title_text, content_texts, levels=None):
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
        title = slide.shapes.title
        title.text = title_text
        
        body = slide.placeholders[1]
        tf = body.text_frame
        tf.clear() # Clear default paragraph
        
        if not levels:
            levels = [0] * len(content_texts)
            
        for i, text in enumerate(content_texts):
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
            p.text = text
            p.level = levels[i]
        return slide

    # Slide 1: Title
    slide1 = add_title_slide(
        "Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks",
        "Time Horizon Doubling Every 7 Months\n\nAuthors: Thomas Kwa, Ben West, Joel Becker, et al. (METR)\nSource: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14499"
    )

    # Slide 2: Methodology
    slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5]) # Title only layout
    slide2.shapes.title.text = "A New Metric: 50% Task-Completion Time Horizon"
    
    tx_box = slide2.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(5.5), Inches(5))
    tf = tx_box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.text = "Methodology involves three steps:"
    p.font.size = Pt(24)
    p.font.bold = True
    
    steps = [
        "1. Assemble a diverse suite of 170 software/research tasks",
        "2. Time skilled humans and measure AI agent success rates",
        "3. Fit logistic model to estimate the task duration at which each AI agent achieves 50% success"
    ]
    for step in steps:
        p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = step
        p.level = 1
        p.font.size = Pt(20)

    if os.path.exists('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_2.jpg'):
        slide2.shapes.add_picture('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_2.jpg', Inches(6.5), Inches(1.5), width=Inches(6.3))

    # Slide 3: Task Suite Overview
    slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
    slide3.shapes.title.text = "170 Tasks Spanning 3 Seconds to 8 Hours of Human Effort"

    tx_box = slide3.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.3), Inches(12.333), Inches(1))
    tf = tx_box.text_frame
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.text = "Task Suite Composition: HCAST (97 diverse software tasks), RE-Bench (7 difficult ML research tasks), SWAA (66 short single-step tasks)\nOver 800 human baselines totaling 2,529 hours collected."
    p.font.size = Pt(18)

    rows = 6
    cols = 3
    left = Inches(0.5)
    top = Inches(2.2)
    width = Inches(12.333)
    height = Inches(4.5)

    table_shape = slide3.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height)
    table = table_shape.table
    table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
    table.columns[1].width = Inches(2)
    table.columns[2].width = Inches(8.333)

    headers = ["Task Family", "Human Time", "Description"]
    for col_idx, header in enumerate(headers):
        cell = table.cell(0, col_idx)
        cell.text = header
        cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
        cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(18)

    data = [
        ["find_shell_script", "3 seconds", 'Multiple choice: "Which file is a shell script?"'],
        ["wikipedia_research", "1 minute", "Research simple factual information from Wikipedia"],
        ["oxdna_simple", "9 minutes", "Detect and fix a bug in molecular dynamics simulation input files"],
        ["munge_data", "56 minutes", "Write a Python script to transform JSON data by inferring conversion rules"],
        ["cuda_backtesting", "8 hours", "Implement custom CUDA kernels for 30x speedup of a backtesting tool"]
    ]

    for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data):
        for col_idx, text in enumerate(row_data):
            cell = table.cell(row_idx + 1, col_idx)
            cell.text = text
            cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(16)

    # Slide 4: Exponential Trend
    slide4 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
    slide4.shapes.title.text = "AI Task Horizon Grew from 2 Seconds to ~1.8 Hours in 6 Years"

    tx_box = slide4.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(4.5), Inches(5))
    tf = tx_box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.text = "Exponential Trend (2019-2025):"
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.size = Pt(24)

    stats = [
        "Doubling time: ~207 days (~7 months)",
        "R² = 0.97",
        "GPT-2 (2019): ~2 seconds",
        "GPT-4 0314 (2023): ~5 minutes",
        "o3 (2025): ~1 hour 50 minutes"
    ]
    for stat in stats:
        p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = stat
        p.level = 1
        p.font.size = Pt(20)

    if os.path.exists('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_1.jpg'):
        slide4.shapes.add_picture('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_1.jpg', Inches(5.5), Inches(1.5), width=Inches(7.3))

    # Slide 5: Success Curves
    slide5 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
    slide5.shapes.title.text = "Success Probability Drops Sharply as Task Length Increases"

    tx_box = slide5.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(4.5), Inches(5))
    tf = tx_box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.text = "Per-Model Success Probability:"
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.size = Pt(24)

    points = [
        "Success rate declines with task length for all models.",
        "Frontier models push the curve rightward:",
        "Claude 3.7 Sonnet: 54 min",
        "o3: 1 hour 50 min",
        "GPT-2: 2 seconds"
    ]
    levels = [0, 0, 1, 1, 1]
    for i, pt in enumerate(points):
        p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = pt
        p.level = levels[i]
        p.font.size = Pt(20)

    if os.path.exists('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_3.jpg'):
        slide5.shapes.add_picture('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_3.jpg', Inches(5.5), Inches(1.5), width=Inches(7.3))

    # Slide 6: Drivers
    slide6 = add_content_slide(
        "Reasoning, Tool Use, and Error Recovery Drive Growth",
        [
            "Key Capability Drivers:",
            "Improved logical reasoning",
            "Better tool use",
            "Greater reliability and self-awareness in task execution",
            "Ability to adapt to mistakes",
            "Limitations:",
            "Performance is notably lower on less structured, 'messier' tasks."
        ],
        [0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1]
    )

    # Slide 7: Extrapolation
    slide7 = add_content_slide(
        "Extrapolation Predicts Month-Long Task Automation by 2028-2031",
        [
            "Forward Extrapolation:",
            "If the trend continues, AI reaches >1 month time horizon (167 work hours) between mid-2028 and mid-2031.",
            "2023-2025 horizon growth rate is ~20% faster than the overall 2019-2025 rate, suggesting possible acceleration.",
            "Caveats:",
            "External validity remains an open question.",
            "Tasks may not perfectly represent the average segment of real-world intellectual labor."
        ],
        [0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1]
    )

    # Slide 8: Implications
    slide8 = add_content_slide(
        "Takeaways: Exponential Autonomous Capability Demands Governance",
        [
            "1. 50% time horizon is a robust, intuitive metric for tracking AI autonomy with R²=0.97 over 6 years.",
            "2. Doubling every ~7 months with possible acceleration since 2024.",
            "3. Current frontier is at ~2 hours of human-equivalent work (o3).",
            "4. External validity remains an open question—tasks may not perfectly represent real-world intellectual labor.",
            "5. Key limitations include poor performance on unstructured tasks and uncertain generalization to real-world job distributions."
        ],
        [0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    )
    
    # Adjust title size for Slide 8 to ensure it fits well
    slide8.shapes.title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(36)

    prs.save('/app/output/final_deck.pptx')

if __name__ == "__main__":
    create_presentation()
